Claude Code, acting on the operator's behalf, was auditing fleet productivity: worker `armor-p6a` (pinned to `~/ARMOR`) was confirmed genuinely productive; four workers pinned to `~/commitgraph` (`alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, `delta`) were either legitimately exhausted (no ready work) or burning cycles in an operator-gated re-verify loop; a roaming worker (`cgov`) was found stuck failing an orphaned-bead release call every ~17-minute idle cycle. The remediation plan was to stop the unproductive workers and relaunch fresh roaming ones.\n10\t\n11\tTwo things happened that didn't match the plan:\n12\t\n13\t1. `needle stop -i alpha` and `needle stop -i delta` each reported `Stopped: needle-claude-code-glm-5-<name>`, but `ps aux` continued to show both underlying `needle run --workspace ~/commitgraph` processes running (PIDs 2244216 and 2248754) after the stop. This reproduces the exact defect plan.md §6.2 / ADR-002 \"Bug 2\" already describes and has planned — but not yet implemented — a fix for.\n14\t2. A subsequent bare `needle cleanup` (no `--all`, no `-i`, intended only to remove the now-orphaned tmux sessions for the workers just stopped) instead reported `Cleaned up: needle-claude-code-glm-5-armor-p6a` and `Cleaned up: needle-supervisor`. Neither was orphaned: `armor-p6a` had a live process actively executing (170+ accumulated CPU-hours at the time), and `needle-supervisor` was the fleet's own auto-scaling daemon. Both tmux sessions were destroyed. tmux's server process then exited on its own — `tmux list-sessions` reported `no server running on /tmp/tmux-1001/default` — because tmux auto-terminates once its last session is gone. This read initially like a wider, unexplained incident; it was fully explained once the actual `cleanup` implementation was read.\n15\t\n16\tSource inspection (`src/cli/mod.rs:1435-1487`) found the root cause. `cmd_cleanup`'s own help text (`\"Remove orphaned tmux sessions (sessions without active workers)\"`) and doc comment (`\"Finds and removes needle tmux sessions that no longer have active workers.\"`) both promise a liveness check. The implementation performs none:\n17\t\n18\t```rust\n19\tlet targets: Vec<&str> = if all {\n20\t    sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect()\n21\t} else {\n22\t    let id = identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"\");\n23\t    sessions\n24\t        .iter()\n25\t        .filter(|s| id.is_empty() || s.name.contains(id))\n26\t        .map(|s| s.name.as_str())\n27\t        .collect()\n28\t};\n29\t```\n30\t\n31\tWhen called with neither `--all` nor `-i`, `identifier` is `None`, so `id` is `\"\"`, so `id.is_empty()` is always `true`, so every session matches the filter regardless of name. **Bare `needle cleanup` is functionally identical to `needle cleanup --all`.** No code path in `cmd_cleanup` calls `scan_needle_processes()` — the exact process-table reconciliation helper `cmd_list` already uses, and the one §6.2's exit criteria commits to building out for `needle status`/`needle list` — to check whether a session's registered PID actually corresponds to a live process. The command's own documentation describes a safety property that does not exist in the code.\n32\t\n33\tNet effect: `needle cleanup` is a hidden `--all` with extra steps whenever a caller omits `-i`, and its output (`Cleaned up: <name>`) is indistinguishable from a genuinely safe, scoped cleanup — there is no signal at the call site that anything destructive just happened to a live process.\n34\t\n35\t## Decision\n36\t\n37\t1. **Implement real liveness-based orphan detection as cleanup's default (no-flags) behavior.** A tmux session is a target only if `scan_needle_processes()` finds no live process backing its registered PID. Reuse this existing reconciliation helper rather than building a second, divergent liveness check — it is the same primitive §6.2 already commits to for `needle status`/`needle list`, so this ADR's fix and §6.2's fix should share one implementation once both land.\n38\t2. **`--all` keeps its current fully-destructive meaning, unchanged.** Its own `--help` text is updated to say so plainly (\"removes every needle session, including live ones\") so the danger is visible at the call site, not only in this design doc.\n39\t3. **`-i <pattern>` keeps its current targeted, deliberate meaning** — naming a specific session by pattern is itself the operator's explicit choice, so it continues to bypass the liveness check exactly as today. Only the no-flags path's behavior changes.\n40\t4. **Update `cmd_cleanup`'s help text and doc comment** to describe the behavior that will now actually exist, and add regression tests pinning all three paths (no-flags-live-preserved, no-flags-all-dead-noop, `--all`-unchanged) so the docs-vs-implementation gap that caused this incident cannot silently reopen.\n41\t5. **Ship through the existing release path**: version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`) — per plan.md's established Deployment convention (§6.8).\n42\t\n43\t## Consequences\n44\t\n45\t- Bare `needle cleanup` becomes safe to run without a manual `ps aux` cross-check first — matches the same trust bar §6.2/ADR-002 already set for `needle stop`/`status`/`list`.\n46\t- No behavior change for `--all` (still fully destructive, now honestly documented) or `-i <name>` (still targeted/deliberate, unchanged).\n47\t- Cleanup's no-flags path now shells out to the same process-scan `cmd_list` already performs, rather than a single `tmux kill-session` loop over every registered name — bounded cost, only paid when cleanup is actually invoked.\n48\t- This fix's implementation depends on `scan_needle_processes()`-based reconciliation; if §6.2's landing slips, this ADR should ship its own minimal PID-liveness check rather than block on it, to avoid leaving the no-flags footgun live in the meantime.\n49\t- Does **not** fix the separate, already-tracked §6.2 defect (`needle stop` leaving orphaned processes behind after reporting success) — that remains open, and is in fact what produced the very \"orphaned\" sessions this bug then over-broadly swept up in the 2026-07-19 incident. The two defects compound: a not-fully-killed `needle stop` leaves a real orphan behind, but an unrelated live session sitting next to it in the tmux session list gets caught in the same net.\n50\t- `needle-supervisor` has no automatic restart-on-crash of its own; recovering from this incident required a fully manual relaunch. Worth a follow-up, not scoped to this ADR.\n51\t\n52\t## Evidence\n53\t\n54\t- `src/cli/mod.rs:1435-1487`, `cmd_cleanup` — full function reproduced above under Context; confirmed no liveness check exists in the `all == false` branch, and `sessions.iter().filter(|s| id.is_empty() || ...)` unconditionally matches everything when no `-i` is given.\n55\t- 2026-07-19 lab incident: `needle stop -i alpha` and `needle stop -i delta` both reported `Stopped:` while `ps aux` continued to show `needle run --workspace /home/coding/commitgraph --identifier alpha` (PID 2244216) and the equivalent `delta` process (PID 2248754) alive, post-stop.\n56\t- 2026-07-19 lab incident: bare `needle cleanup` output — `Cleaned up: needle-claude-code-glm-5-armor-p6a` and `Cleaned up: needle-supervisor`, immediately followed by `tmux list-sessions` → `no server running on /tmp/tmux-1001/default`. `armor-p6a`'s underlying process (PID 1421255, 170+ accumulated CPU-hours) survived independently of its tmux session and continued executing; `needle-supervisor`'s process did not survive and required manual relaunch.\n57\t- Related, already-tracked defect reproduced (not newly discovered) in the same incident: plan.md §6.2 / ADR-002 \"Bug 2\" (`needle stop` not killing the full process tree) — this ADR's Context is fresh, concrete evidence for that still-open item, not a separate finding.\n58\t\n59\t## Addendum (2026-07-21): the shipped fix (bf-1ep0s / commit b5ada58) is itself broken\n60\t\n61\tFound during a plan.md maturity review, before this ADR's Decision had been re-verified against the merged code. `cmd_cleanup`'s new no-flags path (`src/cli/mod.rs`, the `else` branch added in b5ada58) does:\n62\t\n63\t```rust\n64\tlet discovered = scan_needle_processes().unwrap_or_default();\n65\tlet live_pids: std::collections::HashSet<u32> = discovered.iter().map(|p| p.pid).collect();\n66\tsessions\n67\t    .iter()\n68\t    .filter(|s| s.pid.map_or(true, |pid| !live_pids.contains(&pid)))\n69\t```\n70\t\n71\t`s.pid` comes from `TmuxSession.pid`, populated from tmux's `#{pane_pid}` (`list_needle_sessions`, `src/cli/mod.rs:4046,4086`) — the PID of the pane's shell, not the needle binary. `scan_needle_processes()` (`src/cli/mod.rs:4137-4261`) *deliberately excludes* that same shell PID: its own inline comment reads \"IMPORTANT: Exclude shell wrapper processes ... We only want to discover the actual needle worker process, not the shell wrapper\" (lines 4186-4188, 4196-4205), and it returns only the PID of the exec'd `needle run` process itself.\n72\t\n73\tWhether these two PIDs actually differ depends on whether tmux/bash exec-replaces the shell with the needle binary or forks a child for it — this was verified empirically rather than assumed, by reproducing NEEDLE's exact launch invocation:\n74\t\n75\t```\n76\t$ tmux new-session -d -s needle-pidtest \"NEEDLE_INNER=1 sleep 30 2>> /tmp/needle-pidtest.log\"\n77\t$ tmux list-panes -t needle-pidtest -F '#{pane_pid}'\n78\t3322398\n79\t$ pstree -p 3322398\n80\tbash(3322398)---sleep(3322399)\n81\t```\n82\t\n83\t`pane_pid` is the `bash -c \"NEEDLE_INNER=1 ... 2>> logfile\"` wrapper (the output redirection defeats bash's last-command exec optimization); the actual worker process is a **child** with a different PID. This exactly mirrors `launch_in_tmux()`'s real invocation shape (`src/cli/mod.rs:955-971`: `NEEDLE_INNER=1 {self_exe} {args} 2>> {stderr_log}`).\n84\t\n85\t**Consequence:** `s.pid` (always the shell wrapper's PID) can never appear in `live_pids` (which structurally excludes shell wrappers) for *any* tmux-launched session — the liveness check's `!live_pids.contains(&pid)` is `true` unconditionally. Bare `needle cleanup` still classifies every live tmux-backed session as orphaned; the fix does not reduce the 2026-07-19 incident's blast radius, it just changes which line of code produces the same result. `cmd_stop` already solves exactly this shell-vs-child ambiguity via `find_needle_process_in_tree()` (`src/cli/mod.rs:1198-1213`, walks the descendant tree from `pane_pid` looking for the actual `needle run` process) — `cmd_cleanup`'s liveness check does not call it, or any equivalent tree-walk, at all.\n86\t\n87\tNo test caught this because the existing/planned regression tests (ADR-003 Decision #4, plan.md §7.2) test `scan_needle_processes()`'s filtering logic and `cmd_cleanup`'s selection logic against constructed fixtures, not against a real tmux session — the exact indirection that hides the bug. Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n8\t\n9\t1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n10\t\n11\t2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n12\t\n13\t3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n14\t\n15\t4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n16\t\n17\t5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n18\t\n19\t6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## Architecture Overview\n24\t\n25\tNEEDLE is composed of five Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n\n1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n\n2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n\n3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n\n4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n\n5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n\n6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\nNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ JSON value.\n    pub fn to_data(&self) -> serde_json::Value {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": cycle_count,\n                    \"last_strand_evaluated\": last_strand,\n                    \"waterfall_restarts\": waterfall_restarts,\n                    \"restart_triggers\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepCompleted { step, duration_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step, \"duration_ms\": duration_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"elapsed_ms\": elapsed_ms })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerLaunchDeferred {\n                deferred_count,\n                total_wait_secs,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"deferred_count\": deferred_count,\n                    \"total_wait_secs\": total_wait_secs,\n                    \"reason\": reason\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandEvaluated {\n                strand_name,\n                result,\n                duration_ms,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"result\": result,\n                    \"duration_ms\": duration_ms,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                strand_name,\n                reason,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"strand_name\": strand_name, \"reason\": reason })\n            }\n            EventKind::BeadStoreError {\n                strand_name,\n                operation,\n                error_message,\n                stderr,\n                exit_code,\n                workspace,\n            } => {\n                let mut data = serde_json::json!({\n                    \"strand_name\": strand_name,\n                    \"operation\": operation,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"stderr\": stderr,\n                    \"exit_code\": exit_code,\n                });\n                if let Some(ws) = workspace {\n                    if let Some(obj) = data.as_object_mut() {\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Pluggable output backend for telemetry events.\n///\n/// Implement this trait to add a new sink — register an instance in the\n/// `TelemetryBus` and events fan out automatically, with no special-casing.\npub trait Sink: Send + Sync {\n    /// Accept a single event. Must not block indefinitely.\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush any buffered state before shutdown.\n    ///\n    /// Implementations should respect `deadline`: if flushing cannot complete\n    /// within the duration, return an error rather than blocking indefinitely.\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Blanket impl for Arc-wrapped sinks.\n/// This enables Arc<Sink> to be used wherever Sink is required.\nimpl<T: Sink + ?Sized> Sink for Arc<T> {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().accept(event)\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().flush(deadline)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── FileSink ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Writes JSONL telemetry to `<log_dir>/<worker>-<session>.jsonl`.\n///\n/// Append-only, one line per event. Construct a sink using the default log directory (`~/.needle/logs/`).\n    pub fn new(worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n        let log_dir = PathBuf::from(&home).join(\".needle\").join(\"logs\");\n        Self::with_dir(&log_dir, worker_id, session_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Construct a sink writing to a specific directory.\n    ///\n    /// Creates the directory (and parents) if it does not exist.\n    pub fn with_dir(log_dir: &Path, worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(log_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create log directory: {}\", log_dir.display()))?;\n        let filename = format!(\"{worker_id}-{session_id}.jsonl\");\n        let path = log_dir.join(filename);\n        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to open log file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(FileSink {\n            path,\n            writer: std::sync::Mutex::new(std::io::BufWriter::new(file)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Return the path to the log file.\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.path\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file, bypassing the normal channel.\n    ///\n    /// This is called immediately after FileSink creation to ensure that even if\n    /// the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL file.\n    /// The event is written synchronously and flushed to disk.\n    fn write_boot_event_direct(\n        &self,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        Self::write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n            &self.writer,\n            &self.path,\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            version,\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(5), // 5 second timeout\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file with a timeout.\n    ///\n    /// This is a timeout-aware variant that prevents indefinite blocking on hung\n    /// filesystems (e.g., network filesystem issues, stale NFS mounts). If the\n    /// write takes longer than the timeout, it returns an error and the caller\n    /// can decide whether to continue or fail.\n    ///\n    /// The timeout is implemented by spawning a thread to do the blocking I/O\n    /// and joining with a timeout. If the timeout expires, the thread is detached\n    /// and will continue running (and eventually complete or be killed by the OS).\n    fn write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n        _writer: &std::sync::Mutex<std::io::BufWriter<std::fs::File>>,\n        path: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n        timeout: std::time::Duration,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::sync::mpsc;\n        use std::thread;\n\n        let event = TelemetryEvent {\n            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n            event_type: \"worker.booting\".to_string(),\n            worker_id: worker_id.to_string(),\n            session_id: session_id.to_string(),\n            sequence: 0,\n            bead_id: None,\n            workspace: None,\n            duration_ms: None,\n            data: serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_id, \"version\": version }),\n            trace_id: None,\n            span_id: None,\n        };\n        let line = serde_json::to_string(&event)?;\n        let path_for_error = path.display().to_string();\n        let path_clone = path.to_path_buf();\n\n        // JoinHandle::join() has no timeout in Rust's std — use a channel with recv_timeout.\n        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Result<(), String>>();\n\n        // The JoinHandle is intentionally dropped on timeout: dropping detaches the thread,\n        // which continues running until it completes or the process exits.\n        let _handle = thread::spawn(move || {\n            let result: Result<(), String> = (|| {\n                let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n                    .create(true)\n                    .append(true)\n                    .open(&path_clone)\n                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                let mut writer = std::io::BufWriter::new(file);\n                writeln!(writer, \"{line}\").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                writer.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                writer.get_ref().sync_all().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                Ok(())\n            })();\n            // Ignore send error: receiver may have timed out and been dropped.\n            let _ = tx.send(result);\n        });\n\n        match rx.recv_timeout(timeout) {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"failed to write boot event to {}: {}\",\n                path_for_error,\n                e\n            )),\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"timed out writing boot event to {} after {:?} (filesystem may be hung)\",\n                path_for_error,\n                timeout\n            )),\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"boot event writer thread disconnected for {}\",\n                path_for_error\n            )),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for FileSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let line = serde_json::to_string(event)?;\n        let mut writer = self\n            .writer\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"lock poisoned: {}\", e))?;\n        writeln!(writer, \"{line}\")?;\n        writer.flush()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let mut writer = self\n            .writer\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"lock poisoned: {}\", e))?;\n        writer.flush()?;\n        // fsync to ensure durability before shutdown\n        writer.get_ref().sync_all()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── StdoutSink ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Human-readable, color-coded telemetry sink for StdoutFormat::Minimal => {\n                let line = format!(\"{time} [{worker}] {etype}\");\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let summary_part = if summary.is_empty() {\n .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let data_part = if event.data.is_object()\n                    && };\n                let dur = event\n                    .duration_ms\n                    .map(|d| format!(\" {}ms\", d))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let line =      self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shorten the dotted event type to an uppercase action word.\n    fn short_type(event_type: &str) -> &str {\n        match event_type {\n            \"worker.started\" => \"STARTED\",\n            \"worker.stopped\" => \"STOPPED\",\n      \"heartbeat.emitted\" => \"HEARTBEAT\",\n            \"peer.stale\" => \"PEER_STALE\",\n            \"peer.crashed\" => \"PEER_CRASHED\",\n            \"health.check\" => \"HEALTH\",\n }\n\n    /// Produce a brief summary from the event data.\n    fn event_summary(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let d = &event.data;\n        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => String::new(),\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => d[\"agent\"]\n                .as_str()\n                .map(|a| format!(\"agent={a}\"))\n                .unwrap_or_default(),\n            \"agent.completed\" => {\n                let exit = d[\"exit_code\"].as_i64().unwrap_or(-1);\n                let dur = d[\"duration_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n        format!(\"{code}{text}\\x1b[0m\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for StdoutSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let line = self.format_event(event);\n format_duration_ms(ms)\n}\n\n/// Format milliseconds as human-readable duration.\nfn format_duration_ms(ms: u64) -> String {\n    if ms < 1000 {\n        format!(\"{ms}ms\")\n    } else if ms < 60_000 {\n        format!(\"{:.1}s\", ms as f64 / 1000.0)\n    } else {\n        let mins = ms / 60_000;\n        let secs = (ms % 60_000) / 1000;\n        format!(\"{mins}m{secs}s\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Session ID generation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Generate an 8-hex-char session ID.\n///\n/// Uses `/dev/urandom` when available, falls back to PID XOR timestamp.\npub fn generate_session_id() -> String {\n    // Try /dev/urandom (Linux/macOS)\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open(\"/dev/urandom\") {\n        use std::io::Read;\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n        if f.read_exact(&mut buf).is_ok() {\n            return format!(\"{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}\", buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]);\n        }\n    }\n    // Fallback: PID XOR nanosecond timestamp\n    let pid = std::process::id();\n    let ts = Utc::now().timestamp_millis() as u64;\n    let hash = pid as u64 ^ ts;\n    format!(\"{:08x}\", hash & 0xffff_ffff)\n}\n\n// ─── Trace context helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Returns `(trace_id_hex, span_id_hex)` from the current OTel span context,\n/// or `(None, None)` when not inside a valid span.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TraceContextExt;\n    let ctx = opentelemetry::Context::current();\n    let binding = ctx.span();\n    let span_ctx = binding.span_context();\n    if span_ctx.is_valid() {\n        (\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.trace_id().to_bytes())),\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.span_id().to_bytes())),\n        )\n    } else {\n        (None, None)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    (None, None)\n}\n\n// ─── HookSink ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A compiled hook: a pre-compiled regex filter + dispatch target(s).\nstruct CompiledHook {\n    filter: regex::Regex,\n    /// Shell command (empty = disabled).\n    command: String,\n    /// Webhook URL (None = disabled).\n    url: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Dispatches matching telemetry events to external commands and/or URLs.\n///\n/// Each hook has a glob pattern matched against `event_type`. When an event\n/// matches, the event JSON is piped to `command`'s stdin and/or HTTP-POSTed\n/// to `url`. Execution is fire-and-forget — failed hooks emit `SinkError`\n/// events to the file sink but never block the worker or recurse into hooks.\npub struct HookSink {\n    hooks: Vec<CompiledHook>,\n}\n\nimpl HookSink {\n    /// Compile hook configs into a `HookSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if any `event_filter` is an invalid glob pattern.\n    pub fn new(configs: &[crate::config::HookConfig]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut hooks = Vec::with_capacity(configs.len());\n        for cfg in configs {\n            let filter = glob_to_regex(&cfg.event_filter)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid hook filter: {}\", cfg.event_filter))?;\n            hooks.push(CompiledHook {\n                filter,\n                command: cfg.command.clone(),\n                url: cfg.url.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(HookSink { hooks })\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether any hooks are configured.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.hooks.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch an event to all matching hooks (fire-and-forget).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of `SinkError` events for hooks that failed, so the\n    /// caller can write them to the file sink without recursion.\n    pub fn dispatch(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {\n        // Never dispatch SinkError events to hooks — prevents recursion.\n        if event.event_type == \"telemetry.sink_error\" {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        let json = match serde_json::to_string(event) {\n            Ok(j) => j,\n            Err(_) => return Vec::new(),\n        };\n\n        let mut failures = Vec::new();\n        for hook in &self.hooks {\n            if !hook.filter.is_match(&event.event_type) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to command if configured.\n            if !hook.command.is_empty() {\n                match Self::run_hook(&hook.command, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0, // sequence is set by the emitter, not here\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_command\": hook.command,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to URL if configured.\n            if let Some(ref url) = hook.url {\n                match Self::post_url(url, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0,\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_url\": url,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        failures\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a single hook command, piping JSON to its stdin.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns `sh -c <command>` with the event JSON on stdin, waits for\n    /// completion, and returns an error if the command exits non-zero.\n    /// This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is acceptable.\n    fn run_hook(command: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\n        let mut child = Command::new(\"sh\")\n            .arg(\"-c\")\n            .arg(command)\n            .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n            .stdout(Stdio::null())\n            .stderr(Stdio::null())\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n            // Best-effort write; ignore broken pipe if child exits early.\n            let _ = stdin.write_all(json.as_bytes());\n        }\n\n        // Wait for the child and check exit status.\n        let status = child\n            .wait()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to wait for hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if !status.success() {\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"hook exited with status {}: {command}\",\n                status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// HTTP POST the event JSON to a webhook URL.\n    ///\n    /// Sets `Content-Type: application/json` and applies a 10-second timeout.\n    /// Returns an error if the request fails or the server returns a non-2xx\n    /// status. This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is\n    /// acceptable.\n    fn post_url(url: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        ureq::post(url)\n            .set(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))\n            .send_string(json)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"webhook POST to {url} failed: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for HookSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let failures = self.dispatch(event);\n        for fail in &failures {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                hook_error = %fail.data,\n                original_event = %event.event_type,\n                \"telemetry hook dispatch failed\"\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        // hooks run synchronously in accept(); nothing to drain\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Telemetry emitter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Non-blocking telemetry emitter.\n///\n/// Cloning a `Telemetry` handle is cheap — it shares the same background\n/// writer and sequence counter.\n///\n/// The writer task must be started by calling `start()` from within a tokio\n/// runtime context. This is typically done at the beginning of `Worker::run()`.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Telemetry {\n    worker_id: WorkerId,\n    session_id: String,\n    sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,\n    /// Wrapped in Arc<Mutex<Option<...>>> so that `shutdown()` can drop the\n    /// sender explicitly (closing the channel) even while clones still exist.\n    sender: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<mpsc::UnboundedSender<WriterMessage>>>>,\n    /// Pending writer state that needs to be spawned in an async context.\n    /// This is `Some` until `start()` is called.\n    pending_writer: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<PendingWriter>>>,\n    /// JoinHandle for the background writer thread, set by `start()`.\n    /// Uses std::thread::JoinHandle (not tokio::task::JoinHandle) because the\n    /// writer runs in its own dedicated thread with its own tokio runtime,\n    /// ensuring it can process messages before the main runtime's block_on().\n    writer_handle: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>>>,\n    /// OTLP sink shutdown handle (feature-gated).\n    /// Stored separately so we can call its async shutdown method.\n    otlp_shutdown: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<OtlpShutdown>>>,\n}\n\n/// Internal message type for the writer task.\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\nenum WriterMessage {\n    Event(TelemetryEvent),\n    Flush(tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>),\n}\n\n/// Holds the receiver and sinks until they can be spawned in an async context.\nstruct PendingWriter {\n    receiver: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<WriterMessage>,\n    sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>>,\n}\n\n/// Holds an OTLP sink for async shutdown (feature-gated).\nenum OtlpShutdown {\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    Sink(std::sync::Arc<crate::telemetry::OtlpSink>),\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    None,\n}\n\nimpl OtlpShutdown {\n    /// Shutdown the OTLP sink gracefully.\n    ///\n    /// This drains all batched exports before returning.\n    #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        match self {\n            OtlpShutdown::Sink(sink) => {\n                // We need to extract the OtlpSink from Arc to call shutdown\n                // Try to unwrap the Arc - if there are other references, we'll force_flush instead\n                match std::sync::Arc::try_unwrap(sink) {\n                    Ok(otlp) => otlp.shutdown().await,\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\"Cannot shutdown OTLP sink: Arc has multiple references\");\n                        Ok(())\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// No-op shutdown when OTLP feature is disabled.\n    #[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\n    async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Telemetry {\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter that writes to a `FileSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. Call [`start()`](Self::start) from\n    /// within a tokio runtime context before emitting events.\n    ///\n    /// Writes `worker.booting` directly to the file before returning, so even\n    /// if the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL log.\n    pub fn new(worker_id: WorkerId) -> Self {\n        let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        match FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id) {\n            Ok(s) => {\n                // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.\n                // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.\n                // This ensures we have a trace even if the writer thread fails to start.\n                let version = env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\");\n                if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {\n                    // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)\n                    let error_msg = e.to_string();\n                    if error_msg.contains(\"timed out\")\n                        || error_msg.contains(\"filesystem may be hung\")\n                    {\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow\"\n                        );\n                        eprintln!(\"  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.\");\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to write boot event directly to file\");\n                }\n                sinks.push(Box::new(s));\n            }\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n\n        let sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let pending = PendingWriter { receiver, sinks };\n\n        Telemetry {\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            sequence,\n            sender: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(sender))),\n            pending_writer: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(pending))),\n            writer_handle: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n            otlp_shutdown: Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(None)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a telemetry emitter with both file and stdout sinks.\n    ///\n    /// Does not spawn any async tasks. OTLP enabled       → creates OTLP sink with async shutdown\n    /// - Hooks configured   → [`with_hooks`](Self::with_hooks)\n    /// - Stdout enabled     → [`with_stdout`](Self::with_stdout)\n    /// - Otherwise          → [`new`](Self::new) (file sink only)\n    pub fn from_config(worker_id: WorkerId, config: &TelemetryConfig) -> Result<Self> {\n        let session_id = generate_session_id();\n        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();\n\n        let mut sinks: Vec<Box<dyn Sink>> = Vec::new();\n        let mut otlp_shutdown = None;\n        let mut file_sink: Option<Arc<FileSink>> = None;\n\n        // File sink is always created (fallback)\n        match FileSink::new(&worker_id, &session_id) {\n            Ok(s) => {\n                // Write boot event directly to file BEFORE spawning writer thread.\n                // Uses a 5-second timeout to prevent indefinite blocking on hung filesystems.\n                let version = env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\");\n                if let Err(e) = s.write_boot_event_direct(&worker_id, &session_id, version) {\n                    // Check if this is a timeout error (filesystem may be hung)\n                    let error_msg = e.to_string();\n                    if error_msg.contains(\"timed out\")\n                        || error_msg.contains(\"filesystem may be hung\")\n                    {\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"NEEDLE WARNING: boot event write timed out after 5s - filesystem may be hung or very slow\"\n                        );\n                        eprintln!(\"  Continuing without boot event in log file. Worker will still function.\");\n                        eprintln!(\n                            \"  Check: disk space, NFS mounts, filesystem latency, I/O errors\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to write boot event directly to file\");\n                }\n                file_sink = Some(Arc::new(s));\n                // Arc<FileSink> implements Sink via the blanket impl\n                if let Some(ref fs) = file_sink {\n                    sinks.push(Box::new(Arc::clone(fs)));\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create telemetry file sink\"),\n        }\n\n        // OTLP sink (feature-gated)\n        #[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n        {\n            if config.otlp_sink.enabled {\n                // Convert Arc<FileSink> to Option<Box<dyn Sink>> for OtlpSink\n                let file_sink_for_otlp = file_sink\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|fs| Box::new(Arc::clone(fs)) as Box<dyn Sink>);\n\n                match OtlpSink::new(\n                    worker_id.clone(),\n                    session_id.clone(),\n                    &config.otlp_sink,\n                    file_sink_for_otlp,\n                    None, // agent -
